checks.sourceSays: The departmental fee chart is headed "Scale for payable for Registration OR Renewal of the Factory - SCHEDULE -A". It is a matrix whose row bands are installed horsepower ("11-20 H.P", "21-50 H.P", "251-500 H.P", "501-750 H.P.", "751-1000 H.P.", "1001-2000 H.P.", "2001-3000 H.P.", "3001-4000 H.P.", "4001-5000 H.P.", "More than 5000 H.P.") and whose column bands are workers employed ("01-09 W", "10-20 W", "21-50", "51-100", "101-250", "251-500", "501-750", "750-1000", "1001-1500", "1501-2000", "2001-5000", "More than 5000 Workers"), with a separate amount for each three-year licence block ("2023-25", "2026-28", "2029-31", "2032-34", "2035-37"). Worked examples read directly from the chart: at 11-20 H.P. with 01-09 workers the 2023-25 figure is 2506 and the 2035-37 figure is 7158; at 21-50 H.P. with 51-100 workers the 2023-25 figure is 12550.

checks.sourceSays: Note 1 of the DISH/MPOnline process-flow sheet: "There is a provision for deemed approval for this service i.e. in case the officer fails to process the application within the defined timeline (i.e 7 working days), an auto-generated Licence Certificate is issued to the applicant." Note 3 adds: "The Auto-renewal facility is also made available in case of no change of information in existing Factory license." MPIDC's Best Practice 01 note independently lists "Factory License" with "Updated Timeline notified under PSG" = "07 Days" and "Provision of Deemed Approval" = "Yes", and states the reform is "supported by the Madhya Pradesh Lok Sewaon Ke Pradan ki Guarantee (Sanshodan) Adhiniyam, 2021, notified on 3rd April 2021", with "auto-generation of digitally signed certificates ... enabling automatic approval if an application is not processed within the prescribed timeframe."

For "Renewal of License / Hazardous" the same list is extended with "4. Pressure vessel and lifting machine test report issued by competent person, if installed; 5. In case of solvent extraction plant, plant fitness certificate issued by competent person; 6. In case of MAH Unit, proof of submitting updated onsite emergency plan to DIHS office; 7. In case of MAH Unit : Safety Audit Report". For "Form 1A" (plan/layout, both hazardous and non-hazardous) it lists: "1. Flow chart / Brief description of process; 2. Drawings - As per rule 3-A of Madhya Pradesh Factories Rules, 1962, site plan drawn to scale not less than 1:500 and plan, elevation, cross section, of various buildings including all details relating to door, windows, ventilators, emergency exits, lay out of plant & machinery drawn to scale not less than 1:100. checks.primaryClaim: FGD record describes a five-step flow: (1) applicant files online following prescribed document guidelines, (2) department verifies documents, (3) rejected documents returned for correction and re-upload "sometimes more than once", (4) "Physical inspection (not required in every case)" - "One participant's licence was processed without any inspector visit" - and (5) licence issued once documents are in order, with "No detail given on how approval is conveyed". automationLevel is recorded as "partial" and portal.url is null.
checks.sourceSays: The official process flow is a three-step, wholly document-based online process with no inspection step. Step 1: "Applicant applies for License / Renewal / Amendment of License", channel "MP-Online Portal (Self/ MPOnline Kiosks)", forms "Form-1A & 4". Step 2: "Scrutiny of Documents submitted by Applicant - HO / Respective Divisional IHS (Industries Health & Safety) office, securitize all the documents submitted by applicant. During the scrutiny if respective division office finds any shortcoming in the application submitted, they reject the application (Applicant can re-apply in that case).", channel "On Departmental Portal (G2G login)". Step 3: "Issuance of Digitally Signed Certificate - HO / Division Office issues Digitally signed certificate for the desired period as applied by the applicant (Max upto 10 years or more as the case maybe).", channel "Through portal and intimation through SMS/Email." Note 2 adds: "The fees, procedure, and checklist of documents is applicable for all risk categories, sizes of firm irrespective of business location and domicile of the investors." The portal the FGD could not name is the Directorate of Industrial Health and Safety portal at factory.mponline.gov.in, linked from the MP Labour Department site; MPIDC's EODB brochure names "https://labour.mponline.gov.in/" as the venue "For services related to Labour Department (Factory Plan Approval, Factory License etc.)". The portal user manual's own process flow shows the application states "(Sent to Verification, Resubmission, In Process, Approval or Reject) by Director", matching the FGD's report of applications sitting in "verification".

remarks: HIGHEST-VALUE FINDING: the operative Factory Licence service documentation is NOT on invest.mp.gov.in at all. It is published by the Directorate of Industrial Health and Safety (DIHS) on factory.mponline.gov.in, which was absent from the verified source list for MP. It was reached this session by following the live link "Directorate of Industrial Health and Safety" on the MP Labour Department site labour.mponline.gov.in. That portal carries the dated process-flow sheet, the attachment checklists, the Schedule-A/B/C fee charts, the Form 4 user manual and the FAQ - i.e. the four facts the FGD could not supply. labour.mponline.gov.in and factory.mponline.gov.in should be added to the MP source list; note they are distinct hosts from labour.mp.gov.in and services.mp.gov.in, which the earlier pass recorded as unreachable and which still reset the TLS connection when retried this session.

Timeline discrepancy inside MPIDC's own publications. The 2024/2025 documents agree on 07 days: the DIHS process flow (Jun 2024) says "Within 7 days of application submission date" / "7 working days", MPIDC's Best Practice 01 (2025) lists Factory License at "07 Days" notified under PSG, and the EODB brochure's "List of services available on the Invest Portal" also shows "Factory License ... 07 days". But two older MPIDC documents still published on the same domain disagree: https://invest.mp.gov.in/old_portal/wp-content/uploads/2021/06/Service.pdf ("Citizen Charter for Single Window System Services", which states "These timelines are notified under Public Service Guarantee Act") gives "Factory License (under hazardous & non-hazardous category) ... 30 Days" and "Renewal of Factories License ... 30 Days", while https://invest.mp.gov.in/old_portal/wp-content/uploads/2021/06/List-of-services-availble-in-Invest-Portal.pdf gives "17 Factory License ... 1 day". Both are pre-reform 2021 uploads and are presumed superseded by the 2022 'Start your Business in 30 Days' reform, but neither has been withdrawn from the site. The 07-day figure in the MP source list is therefore corroborated, and the 30-day and 1-day figures should be treated as stale.

The sharpest contrast between the primary record and the official position concerns deemed approval, not the timeline as such. The FGD's central complaint is that applications sit in 'verification' indefinitely - "The application is still in verification; it has neither been accepted nor rejected", "The renewal application was submitted in September, but it is still pending" - whereas the official rule is that failure to act within 7 working days should itself produce an auto-generated licence. On the official documents this cannot happen; on the FGD evidence it demonstrably did not happen. This is a statutory-guarantee-versus-practice gap rather than a factual contradiction between sources, so it is not scored as 'contradicted', but it is the finding with the most policy weight.

Fee structure, fuller picture. There are three separate money components and the FGD captured only the intuition behind the first. (1) The statutory licence fee, Schedule A, is a horsepower x workers matrix (confirming the participants' description of "power/electricity-related parameters and employee-related information") priced per three-year block out to 2035-37; Schedules B and C exist as separate charts at the same portal but both RENEWAL_FEE_SCH_B.PDF and RENEWAL_FEE_SCH_C.pdf are scanned JPEG-to-PDF images carrying no extractable text, so their contents could not be read this session and the categories of factory they cover remain unverified. (2) A separate MPOnline portal charge: "Factory Registration / Citizen / 120 / Non Hazardous", "Factory Registration / Citizen / 320 / Hazardous", "Factory License Renewal / Citizen / 20", "Plan Approval / Citizen / 80", with higher kiosk rates and the note "There is no Portal Charge, In case of Resubmission for any type of Application." (3) A late fee: the DIHS FAQ states "a late fee @25% of the fee payable for a calendar year is charged" where renewal is filed after the deadline, renewal being due "at least 30 days before the due date of expiry of the Licence, i.e. upto 1st December of the Calendar year".

Validity, which the FGD flagged as MISSING, is also answered: the process flow says the digitally signed certificate is issued "for the desired period as applied by the applicant (Max upto 10 years or more as the case maybe)" and the DIHS FAQ Q6 states "a factory may get the licence renewed either for one year or up to ten years at a time". Validity is not one of the five scored keys, so it is recorded here rather than as a check.

A material exemption route the FGD did not mention at all: under the "Madhya Pradesh Udyogon Ki Sthapna Evam Parichalan Ka Saralikaran Adhiniyam, 2023", notified 6th April 2023 and live from 11th April 2023, an industrial unit that registers on the single window and obtains an 'Intention to Invest with Acknowledgement Certificate' is exempted from a list of 22 approvals for three years, and that list expressly includes "Factory License - Factories Act 1948 (GoI) - Labour Department" (item 2) alongside "Approval of Factory Plan Layout" (item 1). Source: https://invest.mp.gov.in/wp-content/uploads/2025/01/Best-Practice-02_Exemption-to-Industries-from-taking-approvals-for-a-period-of-3-years.pdf. A reviewer comparing cost-of-regulation estimates across states should know that for eligible new units in MP the Factory Licence may legitimately not be taken at all for the first three years.

Two sources the earlier pass excluded were re-tested this session and still fail identically: https://labour.mp.gov.in/ and https://services.mp.gov.in/eservice/eServices?srvs=4 both return "Recv failure: Connection reset by peer". No workaround was attempted. Separately, the MP Labour Department's Document Management System was searched for a published fee structure and forms: the "Fees Structure" (Sid=21) and "Forms & Procedures" (Sid=6) categories both return "There is no records found", and the "Citizen Charter" category (Sid=16) lists Public Service Delivery Guarantee Act notifications whose PDFs are served only through ASP.NET postbacks, so the PSG notification text itself could not be fetched and the 07-day figure is corroborated from MPIDC and DIHS publications rather than from the gazette notification.

No official gazette copy of the Madhya Pradesh Factories Rules, 1962 could be fetched on a .gov.in domain this session; a web search returned only private legal aggregators, which were not used. Rule 3-A is cited here only because the DIHS attachment list itself quotes it ("As per rule 3-A of Madhya Pradesh Factories Rules, 1962"); no rule number, fee figure or gazette reference in this file has been constructed.
